question.problem: A certain satellite makes $\frac{1}{3}$  of its orbit around the Earth in $\frac{1}{6}$ of a day. How many times can it orbit Earth in $1$ day?
question.worked_solution:
To find how many  times the satellite  can go around the Earth in $1$ day, we can compute the orbital unit rate per day. We do this by dividing the amount of the orbit the satellite travels, $\frac{1}{3},$ by the corresponding fraction of a day, $\frac{1}{6},$ as follows:  

$$
\frac{1}{3}÷\frac{1}{6}
$$

Dividing a fraction by another fraction is equivalent to multiplying the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}÷\frac{1}{6} & =\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{6}{1} \\  & =\frac{1\times 6}{3\times 1} \\  & =\frac{6}{3} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the satellite can orbit Earth $2$ times in $1$ day.
